record_type_quote: Although the data sources are the same (the IDEA Data and the Digest of Education Statistics), the original study relied on data from 2014, while the replication study uses data from 2017.

targets.title: Racial Disparities in Autism Identification in the United States During 2014.
targets.evidence_quote: The claim selected for replication in Travers & Krezmien (2018) is that, compared to California, the odds ratio of autism identification was lower in the state of Ohio.
targets.outcome_quote: The odds ratio is statistically significant at the 5% level (p = 0.000). Thus, this replication of the claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit successful verdict for the selected Ohio versus California claim, tested with 2017 data rather than original 2014 data.

reasoning: OSF GUID resolves to the assigned Travers/Krezmien SCORE final report file, verified by title, focal original and replication team Sisco and Méndez-Chacón. Report lists two replication-team members and dates itself October 27, 2020, whereas supplied metadata lists additional contributors and 2026; this discrepancy is recorded without substituting another work. Different-year sample makes this a replication despite secondary-data design. Original DOI copied exactly as printed, including apparent truncation.
